questions.prompt: What is the dot product of (2, 1) and (3, −2)?

options.explanation: 8 is 2×3 + 1×2. The second product is 1 × (−2) = −2, so the minus sign must stay.
That is the position-by-position product before the last step. A dot product adds those products into one number.
Right. 2×3 + 1×(−2) = 6 − 2 = 4. Multiply position by position, then add.

questions.prompt: Query q = (3, 4). Document D = (9, 12). What is their cosine similarity, and why?

options.text: 1, because D points in exactly the same direction as q.
options.explanation: Right. The dot product is 27 + 48 = 75 and the lengths are 5 and 15, so 75 ⁄ 75 = 1. Cosine ignores length; D is q made three times as long.

options.text: 75, because that is the dot product of q and D.
options.explanation: 75 is the dot product. Cosine similarity divides it by both lengths (5 × 15 = 75), so the result is 1.

options.text: 0.33, because D is three times as long as q, so the score shrinks.
options.explanation: Cosine similarity does not change with length. Dividing by both lengths removes it, so only the direction counts.

questions.prompt: Your vector store holds OpenAI embeddings, which the OpenAI docs say are normalized to length 1. Why can search use a plain dot product instead of the full cosine formula?

options.text: Because the dot product of two length-1 vectors is always 1.
options.explanation: Length 1 fixes the size of each vector, not the angle between two of them. Different directions still give different scores.

options.text: Because both lengths are 1, so dividing by them changes nothing.
options.explanation: Right. Cosine divides the dot product by both lengths, and 1 × 1 = 1, so cosine equals the dot product. The OpenAI docs say the dot product is slightly faster to compute.

options.text: Because the OpenAI docs say cosine similarity gives wrong rankings for its embeddings.
options.explanation: The OpenAI docs recommend cosine similarity. The dot product gives the same scores here; it is only cheaper to compute.

options.text: Because normalized vectors can only point in one direction.
options.explanation: A vector of length 1 can point any way. Only its length is fixed, which is why the angle still carries the meaning.
